cues: A paradigm is a style of organising a program.
Procedural programming is a sequence of instructions grouped into functions, usually sharing global data, designed top down.
Structured programming adds discipline: only sequence, selection and loops, no goto, and modules that talk through parameters.
Object oriented programming organises the program around the data instead: objects that bundle data with the functions that act on it, designed bottom up.
text: A paradigm is a style of organising a program. Procedural programming is a sequence of instructions grouped into functions, usually sharing global data, designed top down. Structured programming adds discipline: only sequence, selection and loops, no goto, and modules that talk through parameters. C is both. Object oriented programming organises the program around the data instead: objects that bundle data with the functions that act on it, designed bottom up.
